statement: The problem of approximating a given element x of a Euclidean space V by elements of a finite-dimensional subspace S, i.e. finding the element of S that is nearest to x in norm.
aliases: best approximation of elements by a finite-dimensional subspace

anchors.quote: Best approximation of elements in a Euclidean space by elements in a finite-dimensional subspace

statement: Theorem 15.16. If S is a finite-dimensional subspace of a Euclidean space V and x is any element of V, then the projection s of x on S is nearer to x than any other element of S: ||x - s|| <= ||x - t|| for all t in S.

anchors.quote: THEOREM 15.16. APPROXIMATION THEOREM. Let S be a finite-dimensional subspace of a Euclidean space V, and let x be any element of V.
Then the projection of x on S is nearer to x than any other element of S.

statement: The element of the subspace S nearest to x in norm; it equals the projection of x on S, minimizes ||x - t|| over t in S, and is unique (equality holds if and only if t is the projection).

anchors.quote: the equality sign holds if and only if $t = s$ .

statement: An element of the (2n+1)-dimensional subspace S spanned by the orthonormal trigonometric functions phi_0, phi_1, ..., phi_{2n}.

anchors.quote: The elements of $S$ are called trigonometric polynomials.

statement: For f in C(0, 2pi), the numbers (f, phi_k) obtained by integrating f against the orthonormal trigonometric functions; they are the coefficients in the projection f_n of f on S.

anchors.quote: The numbers $(f, \varphi_k)$ are called Fourier coefficients of $f$ .

statement: Example 1. The projection f_n of a continuous function f on the subspace of trigonometric polynomials; it approximates f better than any other trigonometric polynomial in S, making ||f - f_n|| as small as possible.

anchors.quote: EXAMPLE 1. Approximation of continuous functions on $[0, 2\pi]$ by trigonometric polynomials.
the trigonometric polynomial in (15.22) approximates f better than any other trigonometric polynomial in S, in the sense that the norm $\|f - f_{n}\|$ is as small as possible.

name_en: Best polynomial approximation by Legendre polynomials
statement: Example 2. The projection f_n of a continuous function f on the subspace of polynomials of degree <= n spanned by the normalized Legendre polynomials; it is the polynomial of degree <= n for which ||f - f_n|| is smallest.

anchors.quote: EXAMPLE 2. Approximation of continuous functions on $[-1, 1]$ by polynomials of degree $\leq n$ .
This is the polynomial of degree $\leq n$ for which the norm $\| f - f_n\|$ is smallest.
